title: Add chaos testing and regression detector to streaming chat load harness
creator: Ava Martinez
description: We need to extend the existing streaming chat/completions load harness to support controlled chaos scenarios and automated regression detection. The goal is to surface regressions in p95 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, and increase in error/abort rates early in the CI cadence and during nightly capacity tests. This ticket covers harness extensions (SSE + WebSocket), realistic token-rate distributions, per-connection multiplexing, KV-cache warmup sequences, backpressure simulation, and an anomaly detector that posts findings to GitHub PRs and the runtime alerting channel. Output from runs should be ingested into a time-series store and compared against rolling baselines to detect both step regressions and gradual drift.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run SSE and WebSocket streaming scenarios at 50k concurrent streams in the staging cluster with configurable qps/token-rate distributions
Collect and store per-second tokens emitted, p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency, connection churn, aborts, and backend GPU token/sec per model variant
Chaos knobs: network latency/jitter (eg. 25–250ms), packet loss (0–2%), delayed KV-cache priming, and simulated slow replicas; knobs are scriptable in the harness
Anomaly detector computes z-score and EWMA-based baselines for p95 tokens latency and flags regressions exceeding configured thresholds (default: z>4 or 20% relative increase)
Automated PR integration: when a performance-affecting PR is opened, CI can run a targeted streaming profile and post a summarized regression report with links to raw metrics and flamegraphs
Dashboard and alert: a per-run dashboard link is emitted and an alert is sent to #runtime-performance when regression is detected
Documentation: clear runbook and run templates for on-demand/cron/CI executions and a small example terraform+k8s config for staging runs
tasks: Design schema for time-series ingestion (metric names + tags) and retention policy
Implement protocol layer for WebSocket keepalive/fragmentation and SSE reconnect semantics
Add token-rate generator with configurable distributions (burst, Poisson, heavy-tailed) and persona presets
Implement chaos injection module (netem profiles, KV priming delays, replica slowdown)
Build anomaly detector service and CI integration hook
Create Grafana dashboard panels and CI summary artifacts (HTML + JSON)
Write docs, runbook, and example CI job for GitHub Actions
comments: 2026-03-10 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after postmortem indicated streaming p95 regressions were missed by existing batch-oriented harness. Proposed adding chaos and trend detection to catch intermittent regressions.

2026-03-11 Ravi Kapoor: Spike completed for WebSocket fragmentation and SSE reconnect semantics. Found race condition when client cancels during initial headers; added a mitigation plan to throttle disconnects during cache-warmup phase.

2026-03-12 Priya Singh: Reviewed anomaly detector design. Suggested EWMA baseline with weekly retrain + a z-score fallback for cold-start. Also recommended storing per-model variant baselines (quantization / sequence length buckets).

2026-03-13 Ravi Kapoor: Implemented Poisson and burst token generators and persona presets (small prompt, long conversation, high-token single turn). Local run shows stable tokens/sec but p95 spikes when KV warmup is delayed by 200ms per request.
